channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett (hip) was a full practice participant on Wednesday.
item.description: Brissett seemingly dealt with an injury in the Cardinals’ Week 2 loss against the Seahawks, but played through it. He opens the week listed with a hip injury but was a full practice participant. Though Brissett seems to have a hip issue ailing him, it does not seem like it will keep him from playing. The veteran remains in the low-end QB2 conversation for Week 3 against the 49ers.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: 49ers WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Robinson suffered an ankle injury in the 49ers’ Week 2 win over the Dolphins. The initial diagnosis was that the veteran would miss some time and his DNP designation Wednesday indicates just that. With Mike Evans (hip) also not practicing, the 49ers’ receiving corps is getting thinner than it already was.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Kupp also opened last week with a limited practice due to the back injury before getting in two full practices and playing in Week 2. His limited designation Wednesday is likely a continuation of veteran workload management for his back; fantasy managers should not be surprised to see the 33-year-old limited on Wednesdays this season.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Commanders RB Kaytron Allen (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Allen popped up on the injury report as a limited participant due to a hip injury. The rookie has seen limited touches as the Commanders’ third-string back and is still buried in the depth chart. Also limited was WR Jaylin Lane (groin). Lane is likely to play as he played through the injury in Week 2. Allen’s status is up in the air; practice reports from later in the week will paint a clearer picture.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Commanders TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and now opens this week not practicing. The 27-year-old suffered the injury in Week 1 and has yet to return to practice since then. The Commanders’ tight end depth chart is thin and neither John Bates or Ben Sinnott are worth rostering with Jayden Daniels out.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw (back/shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Kinlaw dealt with a back injury last week but played in Week 2. He came out of the loss against the Cowboys with an additional injury to the shoulder. Kinlaw’s status for Week 3 is in question as he sits out of practice with back and shoulder issues.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Seahawks RB Jadarian Price (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Price entered Wednesday expected to practice and officially received a limited designation due to a chest injury he suffered in Week 2. Also limited was George Holani (knee). With both backs starting out limited, their Week 3 statuses are up in the air. If one or both can’t go, Emanuel Wilson is the primary beneficiary for fantasy purposes against the Commanders.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Darnold was officially listed as a limited practice participant on Wednesday, returning to practice for the first time since his opening day injury. He split first-team reps with Drew Lock and did some throwing off to the side. The Seahawks will make a decision Friday on Darnold’s game status for Week 3 but the 29-year-old has an outside chance of returning against the Commanders.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Bills DT Ed Oliver (hip) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Oliver suffered a hip injury during warmups of the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions. He did not play in the game and now starts out Week 3 not practice. Oliver could certainly still go this week against the Chargers but he will likely need at least a limited practice to be in consideration to play.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Bills WR Keon Coleman (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Coleman pops up on the injury report with an ankle injury and did not practice on Wednesday. He briefly left the Bills’ Week 2 game against the Lions due to the ankle, but returned and finished the game. Coleman’s status for Week 3 is now in jeopardy; with DJ Moore (shoulder) also on the injury report, the Bills’ wide receiver groups may look slim come Sunday against the Chargers.-Aditya Fuldeore
